system.summary: Numerical syllabary/nomenclator of about 850 numbers, homophones, code names for islands

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out checks, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up. Doubtful signs were settled by targeted visual review where stated.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Key rebuilt from pencil glosses of five 1779 letters of Bouillé (C8 A 78); frozen.
Frozen key on the held-out glossed letter no. 363: 0.865 words / 0.850 characters vs max 0.038 / 0.165 for 200 controls.
Enlarged frozen key K6 on held-out letter no. 415 against its modern translation: 0.894 words / 0.897 characters vs max 0.182 / 0.174.
Letters nos. 238 and 259 and both returns read; returns checked by their sums (1,072 and 4,057 men).

outcome.method_basis: Key rebuilt from pencil glosses of sibling letters (1779), validated on a held-out glossed letter.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 455/458 words read in their sense (437 certain, 11 probable, 7 restored, 3 unresolved).

credits.note: key rebuilt from 1779 glosses, validated on a held-out letter; letters and return read, English translation

texts.label: Bouillé to the minister, 17 Sept 1778 (no. 238), letters of no. 259 and its first return
texts.summary: Short of 817 men, Bouillé cannot attack other British islands after taking Dominica.

texts.label: Bouillé to the minister, 5 Dec 1778 (no. 259) and its two returns (Dominica garrison; troops in Martinique), 9 Dec 1778
texts.summary: Works at Dominica nearly finished; Dominica garrison 1,072 men; troops in Martinique 4,057 present, 1,031 short.
